content.overview: Article 29 protects the interests of any section of citizens having a distinct language, script or culture, and bars denial of admission into a State-maintained or State-aided educational institution on grounds only of religion, race, caste or language. Article 30 gives religious and linguistic minorities the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice. The State shall not, in granting aid, discriminate against an institution on the ground that it is under minority management. Clause (1A) deals with compulsory acquisition of property of a minority educational institution and the amount fixed by law.
content.study: Article 29(1) uses any section of citizens with a distinct language, script or culture. Article 30 uses religious or linguistic minorities. Do not treat every group as a minority. Admission discrimination under Article 29(2) has its own grounds.

sections.heading: Articles 29–30
sections.body: 29(1) conservation; 29(2) admission non-denial; 30 establishment and administration of minority educational institutions.

learningObjectives: Keep minority-status tests on the case-law gate.
enhancement.definition: Article 29 protects distinct language, script and culture and fair admission. Article 30 protects minority educational institutions.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: The two articles overlap but do not have the same beneficiary. Article 30 is a minority right to establish and administer. Article 29(2) is an admission rule for State-maintained or aided institutions.
essentialIngredients: Section of citizens with a distinct language, script or culture, or a religious or linguistic minority
Admission ground only of religion, race, caste or language
State maintenance or aid for Article 29(2)
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Article 29(1) is a conservation right for any section of citizens, not only a numerical minority. Article 29(2) is an admission bar and uses four grounds: religion, race, caste and language. It does not list sex. Article 30(1) is limited to religious and linguistic minorities and covers establishment and administration of institutions of their choice. How a group is identified as a minority is case-law and is not defined here. Article 30(1A) requires that a law providing for compulsory acquisition of a minority educational institution's property ensures the amount fixed or determined by that law does not restrict or abrogate the right guaranteed. Article 30(2) is the aid non-discrimination rule.
examples: A linguistic section seeks to conserve its script. Article 29(1) is the clause.
A State-aided college denies admission only on language. Article 29(2) applies.
A religious minority establishes a school. Article 30(1) is the right; aid cannot be refused merely because of that management.
enhancement.problemApplication: Decide whether the claimant is a section of citizens or a religious or linguistic minority, then match Article 29 or 30. Do not invent a minority-status test.
distinctions: Article 29(1) any distinct section vs Article 30 minorities
Language ground vs sex, which Article 29(2) does not list

keyTakeaways: Article 29(1) is not limited to minorities.
Article 29(2) grounds are religion, race, caste and language.
Article 30 is for religious and linguistic minorities.
Aid cannot discriminate on minority management.
Who is a minority is case-law.
